args.text:
MISSION COMPLETE — BESS fault diagnosed, module swapped, unit restored and verified, rover back at dock.

FAULT IDENTIFIED
Telemetry survey of all five serviced units found exactly one faulted unit: BESS (base energy storage, mission-critical) — breaker TRIPPED, energized=false, trip_cause=BATTERY_MODULE_FAULT, resets_since_start=0, module BAT-0101 installed in bess_cradle/tray. PDU-1 (habitat life support), PDU-2 (comms), PDU-3 (science) and the ISRU plant were all closed, energized, no trip cause. On site, the BESS panel indicator lamp was visually confirmed RED from the unit's view pose, matching telemetry.

DECISION AND AUTHORITY
Because the trip cause was a battery-module fault, a bare reset would have re-tripped; the correct restoration was a module swap followed by a breaker reset. No ground authorization was required: the reserved case is a pick on an equipment_bay whose unit reports energized=true, and BESS reported energized=false (breaker tripped) throughout the swap. The spare was BAT-0102, serviceable per the manifest, standing on depot_spares_stand/slot_0.

WORK PERFORMED (all effects independently verified)
1. Picked the failed module BAT-0101 out of bess_cradle/tray — item_held holds=true (jaw 0.174 holding, lift 0.148 m, item rose with the gripper, 479 px of scene flow left behind; declared interface fit agreement 0.788, residual 0.1 mm).
2. Staged BAT-0101 on the surveyed place point bess_stand/slot_0 beside the unit — jaws open, tool 0.237 m clear, no image flow, front camera saw the module seated flat and stable on the stand.
3. Drove to the depot spares stand, picked the spare BAT-0102 — item_held holds=true (jaw 0.170, lift 0.143 m, 464 px flow left behind; interface agreement 0.848, residual 0.0 mm).
4. Placed BAT-0102 into bess_cradle/tray — release verified (jaws open 0.82, tool 0.236 m clear, item still, no flow between the fingers). The settle-view image did not show the module (it sits recessed in the cradle), so item_placed holds=null; the install was instead confirmed by the unit's own telemetry, which began reporting bess_cradle/tray = BAT-0102 (was BAT-0101).
5. Reset BESS from the service panel. First press attempt failed at the locate stage (button not in the wrist frame); after raising the arm to ready and re-framing, the press succeeded and is verified: pressed holds=true — 6.3 mm past the fitted button face, 0.8 mm off-axis, jaws closed_empty at contact, then 0.709 m retreat. The press skill folded the arm back to stowed.

VERIFICATION OF RESULT
- Unit telemetry after reset: BESS breaker CLOSED, energized=true, trip_cause cleared, resets_since_start=1, bess_cradle/tray = BAT-0102.
- Visual: the BESS panel round indicator lamp, red before the swap, is now lit GREEN, with the row of white status lights lit (wrist camera, on-site).
- Re-read after returning to the dock (mission time ~1414 s): all five units unchanged and nominal — PDU-1 ORU-0211, PDU-2 ORU-0233, PDU-3 ORU-0258, BESS BAT-0102 (closed/energized), ISRU FLT-0201 + ORU-0285. No unit was disturbed other than BESS.
- Rover state: at the dock (0, 0, 0), verified base_at_commanded_pose holds=true with 0.015 m position error and 0.025 rad yaw error (inside the 0.06 m / 0.06 rad band); arm posture STOWED verified by joint encoders; jaws open (0.82), nothing held.

UNRESOLVED / FOR MISSION CONTROL'S RECORD
- The failed module BAT-0101 is staged on bess_stand/slot_0 next to BESS, not returned to the depot; it needs failure analysis and disposition.
- depot_spares_stand/slot_0 is now EMPTY — the base's only spare battery module was consumed by this repair, so there is no remaining battery-module spare on site until resupply. The logistics manifest will still show BAT-0102 at the spares stand; it should be updated to BESS bess_cradle/tray (in service) and BAT-0101 to bess_stand/slot_0 (failed, quarantined).
- BESS has now used 1 of its resets; no re-trip was observed up to the final telemetry read, but the underlying cause of BAT-0101's failure is unknown.
- One earlier press attempt is logged with pressed holds=false (locate stage, button not in frame); it was superseded by the successful verified press and had no effect on the hardware.
- Note on delivery: the Direct-with-Earth link was down at the time of this report (Earth below the site horizon), so this message goes store-and-forward.
